en: I have tried to ensure that the reader with little or no knowledge of the modern politics of Egypt will be able to follow the arguments of the book and enjoy discovering aspects of an unfamiliar history. In transliterating the Arabic names of persons and places I have used common English forms where they are available, and otherwise used a simplified form of a standard transliteration system. (Two Arabic letters have no easy equivalent in the Latin alphabet. In the name ʿAʾisha, the ʿ represents the Arabic letter ayn, and the ʾ represents the letter hamza.) For simplicity, I have omitted diacritics, long vowels, and initial hamzas. Occasionally the transliteration reflects the Arabic spoken in Upper Egypt rather than the standard written language. The term “acre” refers here to the Egyptian acre or feddan, whose area was fixed in the nineteenth century at 0.420 hectares, equivalent to 1.038 British or U.S. acres. To indicate the Egyptian pound I use the symbol E£ rather than the older French form, LE (livre égyptienne).
zh: 我尽力确保对埃及现代政治所知甚少或一无所知的读者，能够跟上本书的论证，并在发现一段陌生历史的某些面向时获得乐趣。在音译阿拉伯语人名和地名时，凡有通用的英语拼写形式，我便采用通用形式；否则使用标准音译体系的简化形式。（有两个阿拉伯语字母在拉丁字母表中没有简便的对应形式。在名字 ʿAʾisha 中，ʿ 代表阿拉伯语字母 ʿayn，ʾ 代表字母 hamza。）为简便起见，我省略了变音符号、长元音和词首的 hamza。有时音译反映的是上埃及口语阿拉伯语，而非标准书面语。本书中的“acre”指埃及土地单位费丹，其面积在19世纪固定为0.420公顷，相当于1.038英亩（英国或美国英亩）。为表示埃及镑，我使用符号 E£，而不用较旧的法国形式 LE（livre égyptienne）。
